This pull request aims to design and implement an architecture by which the handler arguments are validated against its schema before reaching to the backend structure of the codebase.
**Before Implementation**
Frontend data ---> Backend code
**After Implementation**
Frontend data ---> Validation & normalization of arguments ---> Backend code.

metadata.title: Fix #3467: Introduce re-training and add_to_training_queue methods

issue_payload.body:
#3467 

This PR implements two methods.
- add_to_training_queue() method takes an exploration domain object and iterates through all the states in an exploration. It checks for states that can undergo training and then checks if a classifier is present for that state already. If there is a classifier, it checks if re-training is required and creates a job model accordingly . If there is no classifier, it creates a job model. This method will be called within _save_exploration() method whenever there is an update for the exploration.

- check_re_training_conditions() method takes a state domain object and compares the new training data obtained from the state with the old training data obtained from the job. If re-training conditions are satisfied, it returns True. Otherwise, its returns False.

I've also tested both methods adequately covering all cases.

Note: There is a small case that I'm working on - how to handle cases where one answer group is added and another is removed. So, if we get that case working, this PR will be complete.

@seanlip @anmolshkl @prasanna08 PTAL.

discussion_timeline.author: pranavsid98
discussion_timeline.body:
We have with us two lists - 

- state_names_with_changed_answer_groups
- state_names_with_unchanged_answer_groups

Pseudo-code for the whole framework:

1.  create_classifier_training_jobs(state_names_with_changed_answer_groups):
    """Here, we don't really care if there is a previous classifier or not. What we do know is that we need the latest classifier to be trained again. So, if there are previous jobs for previous versions PENDING, they are still trained (used when we revert to old versions of explorations)."""
   
I think the way we have structured the above function right now is fine.

There are a few things we have to think about before implementing the function below that handles unchanged answer groups. First is - if a classifier does not exist for the previous version, there can be only one meaning, which is that the job is not picked up by the VM yet. This conclusion is because, in an unchanged answer group state which passes training conditions here should have passed it in the previous version too, which means there should have been a job created back then. So, going with Sean's concern where we might revert to old versions, I think we can just let the older job store its classifier. So, we need a way to do this: let the older job store its classifier and then map this classifier to the latest version of the exploration.
For this, its slightly weird because we have no way of accessing any ClassifierTrainingJob unless its passed back by the VM or we have the classifier_id. So, we have no way to retrieve the previous version's job, which is an issue here. @seanlip Can we retrieve a ClassifierTrainingJob by its non-key attributes (exp_id, exp_version, state_name)? My suggestion is: have another status called 'OBSOLETE' and mark these jobs obsolete when we handle the case above. If this status is encountered by the StoreJob controller, it also creates a mapping for the <exp_id, exp_version+1, state_name> to the same classifier. This should work (all depending on whether we can retrieve the job by non key attributes.) 

@anmolshkl @prasanna08 I'd need suggestions here.

Thanks

discussion_timeline.author: prasanna08
discussion_timeline.body:
Ok, so the "check" I am referring to is this,
Suppose creator stores new exploration but does not change any answer group. In that case we link this new state to classifier of previous state. Now what if the training job put for previous state is still pending. We don't have anything to map.
So at that time we can obsolete the previous job so that only new one is trained. To find this previous job we have to make query on non key attributes. That's why @pranavsid98 was asking that question. I suggest we do this check, whether a job is obsolete or not, when we perform fetch next job. So no need to query on jobs using non key attribute.

You might ask: how will we link a classifier to previous version? What will happen if creator reverts it back to previous version of exploration? In that case we decided ( @anmolshkl 's idea) that map the classifier of new state to this old state (check that the answer groups are same, ideally this should only happen when old state's job was rendered obsolete. Otherwise all states should have a classifier mapped to them). We need to make sure we are not missing something.

  - That's why we have added the following code snippet so that MyPy can detect the modules we are importing in a file.

        from mypy_imports import * # pragma: no cover # pylint: disable=import-only-modules,wildcard-import,unused-wildcard-import
     ```
  - The part inside the if block only runs when we run type checks. While running type checks, mypy will override the value of variable `MYPY` to `True`. This is substitute of [typing.TYPE_CHECKING ](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.TYPE_CHECKING)in py2.

- I have used self typing in core/storage/base_models. Self typing is giving the type of `cls` or `self` variables so that their type information can be used in type annotations. ## Explanation
<!--

  - when this PR is merged.

This PR aims to include a new stricter check in CircleCI in order to maintain the frontend test coverage stable. The detailed approach behind this new check can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/17x82nghDnmixP30TLQZDVxq_AbGbJuwckp7y0YJ841Q/edit?usp=sharing). The doc separates the logic into two files: .sh and .py. I had to changed it, putting all the logic in only one .py file. CircleCI doesn't check a script error if it's running through a bash file. It works only when executing on .py file.

The stricter check will fail any pull request that decreases a fully covered frontend file. It will be crucial for not letting the coverage drop, after working hard to increase some files coverage.
